---
title: "Composing steps"
---

Steps run in order, and each one selects from the frame as the previous step
left it. That is what lets a later step pick up columns an earlier step
created, and shoez tracks which step produced each column so a selector can
ask for exactly those.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Key points"}
* Steps operate on the output of the previous step.
* `s.has_source(step_type=StepDummy)` selects the columns a step produced;
  `s.has_ancestor()` follows that lineage through later steps.
* `s.has_source("some_id")` selects by step id; a second step of the same
  type is numbered automatically (`dummy_2`), or name it with `id=`.
:::

## Setup

```{python}
from shoez import Recipe, StepDummy, StepImputeMode, StepNormalize
from shoez import Selectors as s
from shoez.data import credit
```

## Each step sees the previous step's output

A selector is resolved against the frame as it exists when its step runs, so
a step placed after `StepDummy` can select the indicator columns it created.
Here the normalize step's `s.numeric_features()` matches the original
numerics and every new indicator column:

```{python}
recipe = (
    Recipe(data=credit, target="Status")
    .add(StepImputeMode(s.nominal_features()))
    .add(StepDummy(s.nominal_features()))
    .add(StepNormalize(s.numeric_features()))
)
fitted = recipe.fit(credit)
fitted
```

## Selecting by source step

Use `s.has_source(step_type=SomeStep)` to select only the columns a step
produced. This normalizes the indicator columns and leaves the original
numerics as they were:

```{python}
recipe = (
    Recipe(data=credit, target="Status")
    .add(StepImputeMode(s.nominal_features()))
    .add(StepDummy(s.nominal_features()))
    .add(StepNormalize(s.has_source(step_type=StepDummy)))
)
fitted = recipe.fit(credit)
fitted
```

`s.has_source()` matches a column's immediate producer. `s.has_ancestor()`
matches any column that traces back to the step, even through later steps
that transformed it again.

## Selecting by step id

`s.has_source("some_id")` selects the output of one step by its id. Every
step has one: it defaults to the step's short name (`"dummy"`), a second
step of the same type is numbered (`"dummy_2"`), and `id=` lets you name a
step yourself.

```{python}
recipe = (
    Recipe(data=credit, target="Status")
    .add(StepImputeMode(s.nominal_features()))
    .add(StepDummy(s.col("Home")))  # id "dummy"
    .add(StepDummy(s.col("Marital")))  # id "dummy_2"
    .add(StepNormalize(s.has_source("dummy_2")))
)
fitted = recipe.fit(credit)
fitted
```
